title: Finite extraction for prime-to-ell decomposed etale families
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning that it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\ell$ be a prime, and let $(u_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose that for every $x\in X$ there are $i\in I$ and $z\in U_i$ above $x$ with $[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$ finite and prime to $\ell$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There is a finite subset $I_0\subseteq I$ such that the same property holds with $i\in I_0$. The sources $U_i$ need not be quasi-compact or separated.

source.place: Expose II Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, for a prime ell; Proposition 2.2.2 makes the prime-to-ell lifting loci open in the compact constructible topology.

proof.text: The finite affine cover in the hypothesis makes $X$ quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Applying the Noetherian closed-subset minimality lemma gives the descending-chain condition on closed subsets. Hence every subset of $X$, in particular every open subset, is quasi-compact. A locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme has spectral underlying space. Therefore the constructible topology on $X$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Expose II Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, using compactness of the constructible topology; Noetherian-to-spectral facts are written out from the cited definitions and existing DAG lemmas.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, put $C_i=\operatorname{dec}_{\ell'}(u_i)$, the set of points $x\in X$ admitting $z\in U_i$ above $x$ with finite residue degree $[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$ prime to $\ell$. Each $u_i$ is étale and $X$ is Noetherian, so the pointwise locus node [lem-per-prime-to-ell-decomposed-locus-constructible] applies and says that $C_i$ is ind-constructible, equivalently open in the constructible topology. This argument does not require $U_i$ to be quasi-compact or separated.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 2.2.2, printed p. 26, applied to each $u_i$.

proof.text: The covering hypothesis is exactly $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i$. By Step 1, the constructible topology is quasi-compact, and by Step 2 the $C_i$ are open in it. Thus a finite subset $I_0\subseteq I$ satisfies $X=\bigcup_{i\in I_0}C_i$. Unfolding the definition of $C_i$ gives, for every $x\in X$, an index $i\in I_0$ and a point $z\in U_i$ over $x$ whose finite residue degree is prime to $\ell$, which is the required conclusion. If $X$ is empty, take $I_0=\varnothing$.

proof_origin.place: Expose II Proposition 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.2.4, printed pp. 26–27; compactness supplied by Stacks Tag 0901.

split_report.summary: Split the ILO finite-extraction argument into the Noetherian constructible-compactness reduction, the prime-to-ell ind-constructible locus for each etale member, and finite selection. Added one statement-only node for ILO II Proposition 2.2.2; the existing completely decomposed finite-subcover item was checked and not reused because degree one is a strictly stronger condition than degree prime to ell. The item statement and hypotheses are unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: The ancestor proof Step 3 uses ILO II Corollary 2.2.4 in its finite prime-to-ell alteration-cover calculus. The three steps realize that finite extraction and its Proposition 2.2.2 pointwise input.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q150-f0747e1f5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and every cited statement against ILO Exposé II 2.2.1, Prop 2.2.2, Cor 2.2.4 and Prop 1.2.7 (printed pp. 26–27). The item statement is byte-identical to the live base node and is exactly 2.2.4 for a prime ℓ. The new node lem-per-prime-to-ell-decomposed-locus-constructible is exactly 2.2.2. Its claim 'equivalently open in the constructible topology' is correct: on a Noetherian X every open is quasi-compact, so with the def's subbase (qc opens and their complements) the open sets are exactly the unions of locally closed sets. I tested the new node on Spec Z[i][1/2] → Spec Z[1/2]. For ℓ=2 the locus is the closed points p≡1 mod 4 and the generic point, of degree 2, is correctly left out; for ℓ=3 the locus is all of X. It also holds for a non-quasi-compact Y. It is true by the degree-sum argument of 1.2.7. Step 1 is the same Noetherian → spectral → compact constructible topology chain as the accepted completely-decomposed sibling, and each cited statement says what the step uses. Step 2's hypotheses match the new node's exactly. Step 3 applies the compactness statement directly; X empty gives I_0 empty. The new node is not a duplicate: no blueprint node (main-20261015 or master) states it, and the degree-one nodes completely-decomposed-finite-subcover and rational-lift-locally-closed-section neither imply it nor follow from it. It is strictly smaller than the item, so this is not a relabelling (D1). It has no SGA citation and no trf node. Its blueprint fields are correct: ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve, via list starting with the item, same_as empty.
